title: Coset quotient, normalizer and fixed functors for split flags
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $B,T,H$ be $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme], let $i_B:B\to H$ and $i_T:T\to H$ be homomorphisms, and let $\pi:H\to Q$ be a morphism of $F$-schemes. Say that $\pi$ represents the fppf coset quotient by $B$ if its natural map from the coequalizer of $h_{H\times B}\rightrightarrows h_H$, given by $(g,b)\mapsto g$ and $(g,b)\mapsto gi_B(b)$, is a sheafification for the fppf topology [def-pc-fppf-site]: precomposition induces a bijection on maps to every sheaf. For a commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $g\in H(A)$, say that $g$ universally normalizes $T$ if after every $F$-algebra map $A\to A\prime$, conjugation by $g_{A\prime}$ preserves the image of $T(A\prime)$ in $H(A\prime)$ as a set. For such a quotient and $x\in Q(A)$, say that $x$ is universally $T$-fixed if for every $A\to A\prime$, every lift $g\in H(A\prime)$ of $x_{A\prime}$, and every $t\in T(A\prime)$, one has $\pi(i_T(t)g)=\pi(g)$. Local lifts exist for the fppf quotient, so this expresses fixation by the canonical left action without choosing the action. A map $e:E\to Q$ represents the closed fixed functor if it is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and for every $A$ and $x\in Q(A)$, universal fixation is equivalent to existence of a unique $y\in E(A)$ with $e(y)=x$. All test algebras, including nonreduced ones, are allowed. Scalar extension of a rational point to a field extension $L/F$ [def-pc-field-extension] uses the unit comparison of scheme pullback, and agrees with the scalar-extension convention [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type].
